newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sets targets for 1996-97 coffee year.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sets targets for 1996-97 coffee year.

text.p: Colombia will produce 12.5 million 60-kilo bags of coffee in the 1996-97 coffee year and 11.5 million bags will be earmarked for export, Jorge Cardenas, the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation, said Tuesday.
He said the production figure would mark a slight decrease from the 12.9 million bags Colombia produced in the 1995-96 coffee year but exports, at 11.5 million bags, will be 7.0 percent higher.

Cardenas's closely watched production and export forecast came in his annual report to the National Coffee Growers' Congress in Bogota where he said he expected the federation's coffee stocks to stand at 5.6 million 60-kilo bags by September 1997, down from 6.1 million for September 1996.
This was based on expected internal demand of about 1.5 million 60-kilo bags during the coffee year, he said.

Cardenas calculated the gross value of production in the 1995-96 coffee year at 1.5 trillion pesos. With adjustments for inflation, he said this represented a 5.0 percent increase over the previous three years.

Based on a projected price of $1 per pound on future markets, plus the $0.13 premium Colombian excelso fetches in New York, Cardenas said he expected Colombia's FOB coffee income to total $1.6 billion between January and September of next year.
He gave no comparative figure for the same period this year but said the slight drop in production in the 1996-97 coffee year was due to unusally heavy rains during the first quarter of 1996.
